content:
Some people find poles help them walk further and more upright.

This guide covers whether they might suit you. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Poles vs sticks

Walking sticks and frames are designed to take weight and support balance. Nordic poles are mainly for rhythm and upper-body work.

Who might benefit

  • People who are fairly steady but want to walk further.
  • People who like a structured walking group.

Grip and hands

  • Choose shaped, padded handles.
  • Use straps so you do not need to grip tightly.

Getting started

  • Ask a physiotherapist.
  • Try a group with an instructor.
  • Start on flat paths.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Can poles replace my stick?

Not if you need a stick for support.

Are there groups?

Some areas run Nordic walking groups.

Sources and further reading

  • NHS: Physical activity guidelines for older adults
  • NHS: Balance exercises
